summary: Kalidas Nag was an Indologist and historian who studied at Scottish Church College and the University of Calcutta. He held positions at Scottish Church College (c. 1915–1919) and the University of Calcutta (c. 1923–1955), and founded the Greater India Society in 1926.

Kalu Rinpoche was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied at Palpung Monastery and Dechen Osel Ling under Norbu Tondrup and others. He served as Vajra Master at Palpung Monastery and abbot at Changchub Chöling Monastery.
Kalyan Kumar Sarkar worked in Indology and Sinology. He studied under Prabodh Chandra Bagchi and served as an Emeritus Professor at the University of Windsor (attested 2002).
Kamal K. Sridhar is a scholar in linguistics and Indology. She served at Stony Brook University as director (attested 2007) and Professor Emerita (attested 2026).

Kamala Tiyavanich worked in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. She studied at Cornell University under David K. Wyatt, A. Thomas Kirsch, and Richard Polenberg, later holding a Mellon Postdoctoral Fellowship there from 1993 to 1994.
Kamaleswar Bhattacharya was an Indologist and philosopher. He held academic posts at Brown University (c. 1968–1970), the University of Toronto (c. 1970–1971), and the University of Bonn.

Kamil Václav Zvelebil was an Indologist and linguist who earned his PhD at Charles University. He held posts at the Oriental Institute, Charles University, the University of Chicago, Heidelberg, Collège de France, and Utrecht University (c. 1976–1992).

Kamlesh Dutt Tripathi is an Indologist who studied under Kshetreṣa Chandra Chaṭṭopādhyāya. He served as professor emeritus at Banaras Hindu University, Chairman of the Kalidas Sanskrit Academy, and Advisor at the Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts.

Kammie Morrison Takahashi is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at Mount Holyoke College and the University of Virginia (PhD 2009) under David Germano, Paul Groner, and Daishun Ueyama.
Kan Hang is a scholar of archaeology and Buddhist studies who studied under Bai Su. He has served as the head of the School of Archaeology and Museology at Peking University.

Kanai Lal Hazra worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and history/archaeology. He studied under Sukumar Sengupta and completed his PhD at the University of Ceylon under Sirima Kiribamune, later lecturing in Pali at the University of Calcutta.
Kanchu Onoe worked in Buddhist studies. He held teaching posts at Hikone Higashi High School (attested 1963) and Eizan Gakuin, where he served as professor (attested 1976).

Kang-nam Oh is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo and completed doctoral studies under Yun-hua Jan, later holding a post at the University of Regina (attested 1990–1998).
Kang-yuan Sung specializes in religious and Buddhist studies. He earned an MA at the University of Calgary, studying under A. W. Barber, Anne Moore, and Leslie S. Kawamura.

Kangei Okamoto was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Takamatsu Yoshie and at the University of Paris (c. 1928–1933). He later held a non-regular appointment at Tokyo National Museum from around 1939 to 1948.

Kanji Tamura is a Buddhist studies scholar who has held academic posts at Rissho University, serving as a part-time lecturer in the Faculty of Buddhist Studies (attested 2001) and as an associate professor (attested 2026).
Kanoko Tanaka is a scholar of religious studies and Indology who studied under Acharya Tulsi. She served as a part-time lecturer in religious studies at Komazawa University (attested 2001).
Kansei Tamura is a scholar in Buddhist studies who studied at the University of Tokyo and served as a lecturer at Rissho University (both attested 1962).

Kapila Vatsyayan was a scholar of Indology and history/archaeology who earned degrees at the University of Delhi, University of Michigan, and Banaras Hindu University. She taught at Delhi and BHU and held leadership roles at the Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts.

Karel Werner was an Indologist and philosopher who studied at Masaryk University and Palacký University under Robert Konečný, Jaroslav Průšek, and Vincenc Lesný. He held posts at Palacký, Cambridge, Durham University (1969–1990), Masaryk University, and SOAS.
